core_obligations: Reduce to the case of the completion B = A^, observing that the henselization and strict henselization cases are handled in exactly the same manner (proof lines 8434-8435).

Let A' and B' be the integral closures of A and B in their total rings of fractions and use the normalization-and-completion lemma to identify B' = A' tensor_A B, hence B'/B = (A'/A) tensor_A B (proof lines 8436-8440).
Conclude the equality of the delta-invariants from the pullback module lemma together with the identification B tensor_A kappa_A = kappa_B (proof lines 8441-8443).
proof_roadmap: Identify the integral closure of the completion as a base change.
Compare the quotients by a length computation.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the delta-invariant of a reduced one-dimensional Nagata local ring agrees with that of its henselization, strict henselization and completion. The proof carries out the completion case and notes that the other two go the same way: it lets A' and B' be the integral closures of A and of B = A^ in their total rings of fractions, uses the normalization-and-completion lemma to identify B' = A' tensor_A B, and rewrites B'/B = (A'/A) tensor_A B (proof lines 8434-8440). The equality of lengths then follows from the pullback module lemma together with the identification B tensor_A kappa_A = kappa_B (proof lines 8441-8443). H2: the base change identification of the integral closures and the length comparison are the substance.
